title: Why two well-behaved agents make one badly-behaved system
question: Why two well-behaved agents make one badly-behaved system
hook: Agent A errs 2% of the time, Agent B errs 3% — and the pipeline they form can fail on a third of its runs.
core_idea: downstream agents condition on upstream outputs as if they were ground truth, so errors don't add — they cascade and compound, and per-agent validation cannot see the interaction term.
visual_object: a relay chain of agents passing a document whose one wrong fact multiplies as it travels
prerequisites: independent probabilities, what an agent pipeline is
exclusions: no resource-exhaustion or authority-laundering modes, no Flux "twin" story, no provenance-tracking design
